cited_details.statement: The literature consistently identifies three mutually constrained desiderata: imperceptibility (the watermarked image must remain visually indistinguishable from the original), robustness (the embedded payload must survive a defined threat model of perturbations), and capacity (the bit rate of the embedded message) [SOURCE 2](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/12/1/74).

The work demonstrated that convolutional encoder–decoder pairs can learn to "use invisible perturbations to encode a rich amount of useful information" into natural images and that, when trained with a differentiable noise layer, the resulting decoder remains accurate against JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, and small image crops [SOURCE 3](https://github.com/jirenz/HiDDeN), [SOURCE 4](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/HiDDeN%3A-Hiding-Data-With-Deep-Networks-Zhu-Kaplan/a4c4c865ed31d88df7458e9f19db54f766f042a1).

The work demonstrated that convolutional encoder–decoder pairs can learn to "use invisible perturbations to encode a rich amount of useful information" into natural images and that, when trained with a differentiable noise layer, the resulting decoder remains accurate against JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, and small image crops [SOURCE 3](https://github.com/jirenz/HiDDeN), [SOURCE 4](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/HiDDeN%3A-Hiding-Data-With-Deep-Networks-Zhu-Kaplan/a4c4c865ed31d88df7458e9f19db54f766f042a1).

It trains a deep CNN-based encoder/decoder to embed 56-bit hyperlink payloads into photographs and reports real-world recovery with 98.7% bit accuracy and 95% hyperlink recovery in in-the-wild videos that exhibit "variation in lighting, shadows, perspective, occlusion and viewing distance" [SOURCE 5](https://papertalk.org/papertalks/15001), [SOURCE 6](https://www.emergentmind.com/papers/1904.05343).

It trains a deep CNN-based encoder/decoder to embed 56-bit hyperlink payloads into photographs and reports real-world recovery with 98.7% bit accuracy and 95% hyperlink recovery in in-the-wild videos that exhibit "variation in lighting, shadows, perspective, occlusion and viewing distance" [SOURCE 5](https://papertalk.org/papertalks/15001), [SOURCE 6](https://www.emergentmind.com/papers/1904.05343).

The work proposes "a novel end-to-end solution for embedding and recovering the watermark in the digital image using convolutional neural networks … and a spreading" transform that improves robustness by trading capacity for redundancy [SOURCE 9](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/b1ffb4adfc9ec647d5dee15cd3dacce1a662ffe5).

The "Hidden in the Noise" line of work on OpenReview proposes a two-stage robust watermarking scheme, suggesting that even richer threat models can be addressed by decoupling the embedding from the noise modelling step [SOURCE 7](https://openreview.net/forum?id=ll2nz6qwRG).

Rather than train a single black-box encoder–decoder, the authors "propose a watermarking algorithm based on multi-scale auto-encoder … which can effectively extract the image feature[s]" that survive compression, and use these features to drive embedding and detection [SOURCE 8](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/ipr2.12961), [SOURCE 11](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374781890_A_robust_watermarking_algorithm_against_JPEG_compression_based_on_multiscale_autoencoder).

Rather than train a single black-box encoder–decoder, the authors "propose a watermarking algorithm based on multi-scale auto-encoder … which can effectively extract the image feature[s]" that survive compression, and use these features to drive embedding and detection [SOURCE 8](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/ipr2.12961), [SOURCE 11](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374781890_A_robust_watermarking_algorithm_against_JPEG_compression_based_on_multiscale_autoencoder).

A 2022 review contrasts conventional and learning-based watermarking along the imperceptibility–robustness–capacity axes and notes that the trade-offs are non-trivial because "regardless of the field or the technology used, there are three common and mutually restricted properties in a watermarking scheme: invisibility, robustness … and capacity" [SOURCE 2](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/12/1/74).

A complementary perspective appears in the SSRN comparative study, which "presented a comparative analysis of traditional domain-transformed watermarking methods and deep learning-based watermark detection models," concluding that hybrid pipelines—where a transform-domain embedding rule is paired with a learned detector—often achieve a more favourable robustness/imperceptibility trade-off than either pure approach [SOURCE 12](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/f8d0a745-298f-46cc-a18f-2f8d4ff89fe2-MECA.pdf?abstractid=6620161&mirid=1).

StegaStamp's print–photography simulation and the multi-scale auto-encoder's JPEG-aware design both show that expanding the noise layer—or replacing it with a learned feature front-end—is a more productive research direction than scaling model capacity alone [SOURCE 5](https://papertalk.org/papertalks/15001), [SOURCE 8](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/ipr2.12961).

StegaStamp's print–photography simulation and the multi-scale auto-encoder's JPEG-aware design both show that expanding the noise layer—or replacing it with a learned feature front-end—is a more productive research direction than scaling model capacity alone [SOURCE 5](https://papertalk.org/papertalks/15001), [SOURCE 8](https://ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1049/ipr2.12961).

**Imperceptibility–robustness trade-offs remain unresolved.** Comparative reviews note that the three classical desiderata are "mutually restricted" and that deep-learning systems have not eliminated, but rather re-parametrised, this trade-off [SOURCE 2](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/12/1/74), [SOURCE 12](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/f8d0a745-298f-46cc-a18f-2f8d4ff89fe2-MECA.pdf?abstractid=6620161&mirid=1).

**Imperceptibility–robustness trade-offs remain unresolved.** Comparative reviews note that the three classical desiderata are "mutually restricted" and that deep-learning systems have not eliminated, but rather re-parametrised, this trade-off [SOURCE 2](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/12/1/74), [SOURCE 12](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/f8d0a745-298f-46cc-a18f-2f8d4ff89fe2-MECA.pdf?abstractid=6620161&mirid=1).

**Hybrid designs are increasingly favoured.** As shown by the SSRN comparative analysis, the most robust results in practice tend to come from pipelines that combine transform-domain priors with learned detection [SOURCE 12](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/f8d0a745-298f-46cc-a18f-2f8d4ff89fe2-MECA.pdf?abstractid=6620161&mirid=1).
The shared HiDDeN codebase has helped in the digital domain [SOURCE 3](https://github.com/jirenz/HiDDeN), but no equivalent standard has emerged for physical or adversarial threat models.

Promising directions opened up by the surveyed work include: leveraging diffusion or other generative priors for perceptual quality, two-stage schemes that separate embedding robustness from detection robustness [SOURCE 7](https://openreview.net/forum?id=ll2nz6qwRG), and learned surrogate models for non-differentiable transforms that would otherwise block end-to-end training.
